pairs.subject: multi-provider-event-normalization
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/provider.rs:177 A string that merely starts with the multi-family host azure is classified as OpenAI before later families are tested, and the price-book fallback then prices that id from OpenAI rows.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/event.rs:160 This crate holds one canonical field per fact. No span-attribute name lists; searched PROVIDER_KEYS, gen_ai.usage, precedence.

crates/core/src/trace_ref.rs:28 The shared door rule lowercases every 16/32-hex id, including the all-zero sentinel, and does not trim or drop empties. Event ids themselves are uuid::new_v4 in new_id.
crates/core/src/lib.rs:6 No provider-response extractors here. usage_split::check_subcounts does reject cached_input greater than input.
crates/core/src/provider.rs:177 Raw ProviderId is preserved and AliasTable is conservative, but azure and vertex are family substrings. vertex is contains("vertex") on the Google arm.
crates/core/src/trace.rs:237 usage_split refuses to invent a token split, and TraceTotals.unpriced_spans labels the detail view. TraceSummary has no unpriced counter beside this f64.
crates/core/src/event.rs:207 received_at cannot be taken from any door's body. normalize_trace_ref is the one trace-id rule both doors are documented to call.

pairs.registryProposal: The technique says both to fold a hosted variant onto one internal provider and to keep the raw string. This code stores the raw canonical id and uses family only as a price-book fallback; the standard should say whether that split is conforming, apart from the host-substring ban it already states.

crates/gateway/src/telemetry.rs:79 One native JSON emission path. This crate is not an ingest operator adding a second wire format.

pairs.subject: multi-provider-event-normalization
pairs.evidence: clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:46 Host names that front more than one model family are rewritten to a single lab before the event is sent, and the original provider string is not kept.

techniques.evidence: clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:75 Reads a provider response object, not span attributes. Searched gen_ai, otel, opentelemetry, span_attribute under clients/python: no hits. Name fallbacks belong to the extractor technique.
clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:10 track() never sets id, including when it sends trace_id and span_id. Journal recovery re-posts the same span under a new server-minted id.

clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:96 Three extractors share _get and return one tuple. Anthropic adds cache read and cache write into input and keeps the read as cached_input, which stays None when absent. OpenAI tries prompt_tokens before input_tokens.
clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:46 Unknown names pass through _PROVIDER_ALIASES.get verbatim. azure, vertex, and genai are folded, so a multi-family host becomes one lab.
clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:305 Omitted counts become 0, including journal recovery, whose log says the tokens are unknown. A missing model is sent as the string unknown.
clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:576 One native event path. Guard scores post to /v1/scores and are not a second event format.

pairs.registryProposal: per-provider-usage-extractors requires a stated fallback order for naming duals but does not say newest-first, while attribute-precedence-lists does. The OpenAI extractor tries prompt_tokens before input_tokens; if a dual-emitting response should prefer the current name, the extractor technique should say so.
